statement: The organising of the 705 rooms sorts into 197 kinds of doing (183 on the main tier, 14 rare), and no kind holds more than 7% of the 7,786 placed second-order themes. Half of those themes (51.1%) carry one kind; the rest carry two (25.3%) or three (23.6%). Themes about dealing with other rooms (borders, truces, alliances, help, restraint) carry the most kinds at once: 36.0% of them sit on one kind, against 54.1% of the others.
bound: One reader's placements of the 7,786 second-order themes, before any fresh reader tested the gates. The share of themes that need two or three kinds rises with the grain of the second-order theme: 70.4% sit on one kind at five concepts or fewer, 35 to 38% at six to twenty. The share therefore measures the A1 coders' cut as well as what the rooms did.
refuted_by: Fresh readers at stage B2, holding the gates, disagree on the primary kind in more than a third of the second-order themes they place; or merging the dealing kinds (T3-010 with T3-149, T3-150 and T3-151) loses no distinction those readers draw.

Within a room, larger second-order themes carry more kinds (mean within-room Spearman 0.28 between a theme's concepts and its kinds, positive in 482 of 619 rooms; themes of five concepts or fewer sit on one kind 16 points above their room's own share). Across rooms, a room's grain predicts nothing (Spearman -0.08 between a room's mean concepts per theme and its single-kind share, 633 rooms). The B1e line said the share measures the A1 coders' cut and that grain separates canucks from turkey; that does not hold across rooms and is withdrawn.

why: the PI pointed out (2026-10-11, from the B1e interview) that the grain bound does not hold across rooms; b2_grain_check.py confirms it, and the bound is rewritten to the within-room relation the data show

statement: After a room moves its work, calls and build reports come later less often than a shuffle of the room's own concepts predicts: some call follows the first move in 57 of 79 rooms carrying both (0.722, null mean 0.962) and some build report in 49 of 65 (0.754, null mean 0.939). A move returns a room to choosing a spot more than to recruiting.
bound: A corpus rate, not a claim about each room: four of the twenty pass 1 story rooms (day9, texas, scp, worldoftanks) called members in again after a loss; open in out/_questions/relocation-renewed-calls.md.

statement: day9 stopped organizing early, its last coordinating turn at h53.3, because its second work was finished and held after a move ('The new location is finished!', h53.1), not because the room gave up; a member named a diplomat at h55 and another recounted the week at the close.
bound: One room; the stop is read from its forest and the A1 organizing end.

statement: The close runs in order: a reported build comes before the first celebration in 182 of 282 rooms carrying both (0.645, null mean 0.433), a celebration before the first record in 225 of 289 (0.779, null 0.565), and a record before the first plan to carry on in 113 of 145 (0.779, null 0.563).
bound: On the late side the record often comes first (8 of 15 rooms hold for celebration then record); carrying on can begin while the work stands (texans).

statement: Machine hands arrive under strain: in rooms carrying both, upkeep comes before the first script or spare account in 160 of 203 (0.788, null mean 0.603), and the reverse order holds in 41 of 203 (0.202, null mean 0.375).
bound: Where a room scripted the building or an attack from the start, machine hands come first (canucks, empiredidnothingwrong).

statement: Decided order is rare: a decided element of order (a leader, a vote, an oath, a sanction, a division of the work; Decided order) is placed in 46 of 705 rooms, against 526 for repair work and 522 for the completion ritual.
bound: Counts placed themes; votes and divisions of work also appear in rooms not placed on it (sweden, ripcity, edmontonoilers, empiredidnothingwrong in the pass 1 story rooms).

statement: A move lowers a room's calling and building from the crisis before it, but not below other rooms: a call falls in the six hours after the first move in 29 of 74 rooms (0.392), against 37 of 74 in the six hours before (0.500) and 0.290 for other rooms at the same hours; a build report in 19 of 60 (0.317), against 0.417 before and 0.309 for other rooms.
why: Pass 1's statement (calls after a move rarer than a shuffle predicts, against a null of 0.962) set a bar raised by rooms dense in calls; four of the twenty pass 1 story rooms called again after a loss; the window test declared at pass 2 replaces it (c2_relocation_window-p2.txt).
bound: A move is followed by fewer calls than the crisis before it; it does not stop a room from calling.

statement: A room's own call to attack is answered inside the room: in 82 of 104 rooms carrying both, the first attack call comes before the first sparing, refusal or apology (0.788 against a null mean of 0.529), and in 95 of 172 before the first border talk (0.552 against 0.423).
bound: Reining in needs an attack to rein in, so the first share is partly constitutive; on the late side border talk comes first (0 of 4).

statement: Short of hands, rooms turn to other rooms: in 171 of 240 rooms carrying both, the first upkeep comes before the first help given, asked for or traded with another room (0.713 against a null mean of 0.596), and in 106 of 157 before the first coalition (0.675 against 0.569).
bound: Late rooms often enter the canvas through other rooms, with help or a coalition first (A19 holds in 2 of 7 late rooms).

statement: The play frame does not delay the canvas work across rooms: 59 frame-filled rooms at held size start their canvas work at a median h21.80, against h20.25 for 275 others (one-sided permutation p 0.43, 2,000 permutations).
bound: A first run that counted only cited frame concepts put 8 rooms in the group and found a 15.5-hour delay; the rule undercounted the frame and was corrected before the result was used. ultrahardcore and totallynotrobots started late inside the frame; they are not its rule.

statement: Calls to the canvas bring the host sub's line around canvas talk: in 132 of 155 rooms carrying both, the first call comes before the first megathread, removal by rule, changed rule, canvas sub, objection to the flood or dismissal of the canvas (0.852 against a null mean of 0.538, p95 0.594); early side 48 of 57, late side 2 of 2.
bound: Partly constitutive: a removal or an objection needs canvas posts. 23 rooms draw the line first: rules remove the first call as it is posted (9), a canvas sub or megathread is set up before the host carries a call (7), members dismiss the canvas or object to other rooms' canvas posts before the room calls (7).

statement: Membership carried in does not come before the attack more than chance: in 86 of 145 rooms carrying both, the first concept of the body carried in (a nation's flag and history, a colour, the sub's quarrel, lore, jokes or ideology; 22 third-order themes) comes before the first attack (0.593 against a null mean of 0.580, p95 0.634).
bound: The quarrel theme alone failed at pass 2 (2 of 9 rooms). The story rooms show membership framing a fight after it (a fight told as national history); that order was not tested.

statement: Hosting follows neither exchange, coalition nor upkeep: help between rooms comes first in 11 of 29 rooms carrying both (0.379, p95 0.552), a coalition in 5 of 17 (0.294, below the null mean of 0.451), upkeep in 33 of 52 (0.635, p95 0.654). Where hosts give a ground for a ruling on a request to build, it is space or design in 12 of 23 concepts, fit with the body in 6 and ties in 5. The six rooms whose own rulings are cited all have an empty pre-event brief; the seventh room with a cited ruling (yugioh) carries a host's ruling on itself.
bound: Membership then hosting beat the null (21 of 28 rooms, 0.750 against p95 0.714, thin) but is not an arrow: the declared mechanism (guests come to the body's mark) shows in 5 of the 21 rooms, and 16 show the reverse role, a room asking a host for space after laying its own mark (c2_first_concepts-K04-P19-p3.txt). The ruling reading covers only the concepts cited under vetting others' requests (61 in 7 rooms); national hosts' rulings coded under other themes are not in it.

refuted_by: a room where the host sub's first line answers no call or flood while the canvas runs

statement: In some rooms a tie the members had before the canvas names the rival in the same turn that calls for or carries out the attack. Read in the story rooms of passes 1 to 4, 10 turns in 7 rooms pass three checks (an attack called or carried out, the rival named, the tie named or rested on in the words): CKCrusaders, anarcho_capitalism, cardinals, completeanarchy, lakers, rpi, unitedkingdom. Examples: "For two world wars the French and british have stood together against the germans ... covering the flag of Germany" (unitedkingdom/c0146); "You mean WPI? I'm down for a lil interpolytechnic griefing." (rpi/c0022); "Proposal: CRUSADE against the infidel. Recapture Constantinople ... The flag of Turkey is bottom left from us, let's conquer it." (CKCrusaders/c0085).
bound: Untested for order (QC2-002): the tie and the attack are one turn, so no order statement can count it, and no share of rooms is claimed. The coders placed these turns under the attack and taunt themes; in lakers, rpi and cardinals no concept sits under the membership candidate's themes. Colour factions the canvas gathered name rivals the same way (5 turns in 3 rooms) and are reported as a boundary, not as this finding, since their faith is not a tie from before the canvas.
refuted_by: a reading in which the cited turns' rivals were chosen by the canvas (neighbours, attackers) and the named tie only dresses the choice: the rival named in the turn is the room's nearest neighbour or its attacker, not a rival known before the canvas
why: pass 5, declaration 3: J's ruling on QC2-002

statement: Decided order is rare: a decided element of order (a leader, a vote, an oath, a sanction, a division of the work; Decided order) is placed in 46 of 705 rooms, against 526 for repair work and 522 for the completion ritual.
bound: Counts placed themes; votes and divisions of work also appear in rooms not placed on it (sweden, ripcity, edmontonoilers, empiredidnothingwrong in the pass 1 story rooms). Bounded at C3a by an abductive read prompted by O'Mahony and Ferraro 2007, who hold that a production community establishes a shared basis of authority before it can govern itself (p. 1081). Decided order gathers where a room governs a territory for a colour or rules on guests' requests to build: 7 of the 39 rooms placed on a colour-faction theme (Neo-tribes) or on vetting others' requests carry it (0.179), against 39 of the 666 other rooms (0.059). Held to room size, 7 against a null mean of 2.7 (95th percentile 5, p 0.0140; decided-order rooms shuffled within items_in_window quartiles, 2000 shuffles, seed 20261014). The gap lies in the two smaller quartiles (5 of 14 against 13 of 339); in the two larger it vanishes (2 of 25 against 26 of 327). None of the 56 rooms whose members asked a host for space carries it. The factions appoint overseers and lay down rules (PurplePixels c0057, c0137), name a temporary leader (TheGreatGreenBox c0051) and call for bans (orderofthebluecorner c0009).
why: stage C3a, contradicting work: O'Mahony and Ferraro 2007; the disagreement is about the setting and bounds the claim to rooms whose work is their own picture

statement: Refusals of a call carry a reason; acceptances come bare. Of 80 seeded reply pairs, 57 had a first part that calls for or proposes an attack. Read for stance, refusals gave a reason in 23 of 38 and acceptances in 2 of 14 (one-sided Fisher p 0.0032). Refusals were not longer (median 9.5 words against 11.5). In a refusal the reason states the room's norm or the attack's cost: 'Why? That'll just cause them to want to attack us' (uoft/c0115).
bound: Coded by the analyst alone under rules written before reading. First parts are attack calls only; calls to place were not tested. The theme a reply sits under does not track its stance, so the pairs were drawn by theme and coded by reading. Reply intervals were not read as conversation analysis's delay, since posting latency is not turn-internal delay.
refuted_by: a second coder, reading the same pairs under the same rules, finding reasons about as often in acceptances as in refusals
why: stage C3b, section 4a: the distant field's prediction for the call and its answers, tested

statement: The rooms do not read their numbers off the replies to a call (weak: an absence claim). Of 40 seeded first turns on the doubt-about-numbers theme, 11 judge the room's own hands, and 0 of them rest on who answered or is present in the thread. 3 rest on the size of the sub, fan base or game, 2 on the canvas, 1 on both, and 5 on nothing: 'Sadly I don't think we have enough people to make anything :(' (sabres/c0008).
bound: Coded by the analyst alone; one theme, one sample of 40 rooms. The readership ground was not foreseen when the rules were written and is coded apart. A thread ground does appear outside the sample: 'I mean I want to but nobody's here' (torontoraptors/c0060), in reply to an attack call. The claim is about small rooms writing in public and is marked weak.
refuted_by: a wider read of judgments of numbers in which a clear share cite the replies or the people present
why: stage C3b, section 4b: the concept's claimed function (the replies as the room's head count) tested against the threshold models' prediction

statement: Nine of the 28 fourth-order themes are ways of handling one of the four universal problems, and 19 are not. Information provision: 4 themes (Sensemaking, Stigmergy, Backstage decision-making, Attribution), 555 of 705 rooms. Reward provision: 2 (Completion ritual, by construction; Visibility returns), 543 rooms, nearly all of it credit and celebration after the work; a reward offered before the work appears in 9 rooms (prizes 7, a tile as payment 2). Task allocation: 2 (Mobilization, by construction; Decided order), 394 rooms; by self-selection to calls in 361 (calling members 345, recruiting kindred subs 44, timing a mass placement 2), by decision in 46. Task division: 1 (Standardization of output), 237 rooms, by coordinates and templates (207); division among teams in 5. The remainder of 19 holds 7 themes between rooms (a change of level), 6 that make the boundary and membership the frame takes as given, 3 different mechanisms (making the goal, sizing it, multiplying hands under the rate limit), the work itself (repair), and 2 after the clock.
bound: The mapping is the analyst's reading of the declarations as they stood, one reader. The counts are rooms whose coded talk sits under a theme, not rooms that solved a problem: the evidence is talk in public and there is no denominator of groups (contract section 5). Two mappings are by construction (Mobilization, Completion ritual) and rest on the declarations, not on the rooms showing that a call allocated or that credit induced anyone to place. Every claim that a problem is absent or thin is about small rooms writing in public and is marked weak.
refuted_by: a second reader mapping the 28 declarations and placing most of the remainder under one of the four
records of the chats showing that most rooms assigned parts or promised rewards where the threads are silent
why: stage C3c, section 5: the contract's section 1 claim put to the structure as it stands, not revised to fit

statement: The rooms' goals were made on the clock, mostly from a sign the room already had, proposed by one member and argued in its design rather than chosen between; a vote was rare; loss changed the goal. A member proposes the room's mark in 166 of 705 rooms (median first hour 12.7). The design is argued in 281 rooms and put to a vote in 18 (median first vote at hour 42.4; 7 of 18 before hour 24). The goal is inherited in 152 rooms: the homeland's flag 96, national emblems 39, the room's mark found already placed 43, a sign others began adopted 6. It is contested in 152, mostly over whether the canvas belongs in the host sub at all (arguing the canvas's worth 76, objecting to the canvas flood 72). It is changed in 190: relocating 116, upkeep chosen over expansion 43, fewer pieces 29, quitting 20, weighing fight against move 17. The structure places the making of the goal in Collective representation (T4-006) and the model in the room settling its mark (P02) and the starter (R01), outside the four problems, which take the goal as given. The goal is a picture, so one artifact can state it and divide it (A11, theorised); at room level an argued design goes with shared coordinates only slightly more often (94 of 281 rooms, against 113 of the other 424; not held to size).
bound: The four modes are the analyst's placement of third-order themes by their names; the theme a record sits under does not track its stance, so the counts are of rooms whose coded talk sits under a theme, not of rooms read for how they chose. The modes overlap (a room can inherit a flag and argue its design). Counts are not held to size. A goal set in a chat or before the canvas is invisible here, and the claim that goals were rarely chosen between rivals is an absence claim, marked weak.
refuted_by: a read of the rooms' first proposals showing that most goals were chosen against a rival proposal, or set by a body outside the room
why: stage C3c, section 5, part 5: whether each room inherited, negotiated, contested or changed its goal, the question C3a left open from Felin and Zenger

statement: Stigmergy's cut joined two kinds of record. Three readers coded the 72 records drawn at C5a-01 from its three member themes, each record taking the code two of them gave. Building and reporting the mark (T3-038) reports the work's state in 10 of its 14 records that bear on the work. Extending the room's work (T3-041) proposes or asks what to add in 8 to 10 of 15, and adding a personal piece (T3-060) in 10 of 20. By the rule written before the read, the second two moved to Collective representation at C5c-02, and Stigmergy holds building and reporting alone.
bound: Three coders and 24 records per theme. Agreement is moderate: mine and the fleet reader's 57 of 72 (kappa 0.69), mine and the field analyst's 47 (0.47), the fleet reader's and the field analyst's 48 (0.50). T3-060 meets the rule at exactly half, and the field analyst's codes alone would leave it (9 of 19). The record holds the talk, not the placing.
refuted_by: a larger coded draw in which proposals fall below half of the bearing records of extending the work and of adding a personal piece
why: J's ruling 3 of 15 October: recut Stigmergy only if the cut joins what Grassé and Heylighen keep apart; the fleet readers at C5c-01 and the field analyst at C5c-02 coded blind, and the rule, its destinations and the three-coder combination were logged before each tally

statement: After a loss, a room that judges its hands too few either moves or gives the work up. Of the 21 rooms carrying both doubt about their hands (K02) and a move (P10), read whole, 10 voiced the judgment before the move, after a loss or erosion of the spot ('We just don't have the people.' [anarcho_capitalism/c0031], then 'Building ancap flag somewhere else would be a good idea' [anarcho_capitalism/c0077]); in 10 the loss itself prompted the move, and the judgment came after it or inside the move turns; 1 did not move. Of the 36 rooms that voiced such doubt and whose record says the work was lost, 10 moved, and of the 26 with no move, 11 gave the work up ('we're not doing this anymore don't do it' [raocow/c0062]), 7 voiced the doubt before any loss and 8 otherwise.
bound: Coded by the analyst alone under rules written before reading; the first three concepts of each element in each room. 10 of 20 is at the rule's line; read as a coalition's move, MiamiHurricanes makes it 9 of 20, where the rule does not decide. The judgment speaks for the room in 7 of the 10 and for one member apart in 3. work_remained is what the room's record says, not the canvas.
refuted_by: a second coder, reading the same rooms under the same codes, finding the judgment before the move in fewer than a third of the rooms that moved after a loss
prompted_by: J's advice on thin evidence (C5c-07): crucial things happen rarely
why: problem 3 of the serial work (notes-C5.md, C5c-07 and C5c-08): A10 was thin on 21 rooms; every room was read whole, and the rooms that voiced doubt, lost their work and did not move were read for what they did

statement: Sparing a neighbour rests mostly on the room's own norm; help between rooms rests on a deal about as often as not. Read whole, the first sparing concept names a border, truce, deal, policy or agreement in 17 of the 124 rooms where it is the room sparing a neighbour (11 of 81 where border talk comes first, 6 of 43 where it does not); the rest state a norm ('Don't ruin other people work' [czech/c0062]), refuse a raid or apologise. The first help between rooms names a deal, border, truce, alliance, an exchange or the neighbour relation as its ground in 86 of 194 rooms: 63 of 127 where border talk comes first, against 23 of 67 where help comes first ('As per the terms, we will help with the triangle' [TeamYellowPlace/c0047]).
bound: Coded by the analyst alone under rules written before reading; the first concept of each element in each room. A later sparing or help concept may name a deal the first does not. Kin ties ('brothers') were counted as help with no ground, since they come from before the canvas. For help, 63 of 127 (0.496) falls between the half and the third that the rule written first set, so whether the mechanism shows in words is my judgment, made on the contrast with rooms where help came first.
refuted_by: a second coder finding the line named in sparing about as often as the channel in help, or the channel named as often where help comes first as where border talk does
prompted_by: J's advice on thin evidence (C5c-07): look at the evidence again
why: problem 3 of the serial work: A05 and A14 were thin by their order counts; every room carrying both elements was read whole for whether the mechanism shows in the members' words

statement: Most rooms that called for hands report a work up after the call. Of 370 rooms carrying calls for hands (P01), 284 carry a report that a work is up (P11), and in 233 (0.630) the first such report comes after the first call. The share rises with the room's size: 24 of 60 rooms with calls in the smallest quarter by items in the window, 55 of 90, 74 of 110, and 80 of 110 in the largest.
bound: First cited concepts by hour, as in the order tests; no null is drawn, so this is a share, not an order beating chance. A report that the work is up is the room's own word in its record; it does not show who placed the pixels, and much of a room's artwork was placed by people who never wrote in it. The canvas is not evidence (rule 7). A room that writes more carries more elements, which the size gradient may partly reflect.
refuted_by: a reading of the reports that finds most of them announce a work begun or planned rather than one up
prompted_by: J's guidance on 'aligned' (C5c-07); Okhuysen and Bechky 2009, p. 469: across definitions, coordination means that 'a goal, task, or piece of work is achieved'
why: problem 4 of the serial work: whether D02 and the alignment proposition may say that rooms aligned many hands, or only that members tried; the rule logged first said 'aligned' of the rooms whose record reports the work built after the call, with its count

statement: Reports of the work's state and templates are carried largely apart. Building and reporting the mark (T3-038) is carried by 237 rooms and the members of Standardization of output (T4-008) by 237; 89 carry both, about what independence would give (80), and 385 carry either. So 148 rooms report the state of their mark with no template or coordinates coded, and 148 share templates with no report coded.
bound: Rooms carrying a theme's cited concepts. A room in which no report was coded may still have reported its work in talk the coders placed elsewhere; the counts say what the coded record carries.
refuted_by: a recount in which most rooms that share templates also report the state of their mark
prompted_by: the weighing of option (d) at C5c-10: whether reports and templates are one coordinating route
why: problem 4 of the serial work: a merge of Stigmergy and Standardization of output would join two routes that the coded rooms carry apart and that the C3 mapping assigns to different universal problems

statement: Stigmergy's cut joined two kinds of record. Three readers coded the 72 records drawn at C5a-01 from its three member themes, each record taking the code two of them gave. Building and reporting the mark (T3-038) reports the work's state in 10 of its 14 records that bear on the work. Extending the room's work (T3-041) proposes or asks what to add in 8 to 10 of 15, and adding a personal piece (T3-060) in 10 of 20. By the rule written before the read, the second two moved to Collective representation at C5c-02, and the theme holds building and reporting alone; since C5c-10 it is named Direct information sharing (T4-007).
bound: Three coders and 24 records per theme. Agreement is moderate: mine and the fleet reader's 57 of 72 (kappa 0.69), mine and the field analyst's 47 (0.47), the fleet reader's and the field analyst's 48 (0.50). T3-060 meets the rule at exactly half, and the field analyst's codes alone would leave it (9 of 19). The record holds the talk, not the placing. At C5c-10 the recut stands and the theme was renamed: its records are members' posts of the work's state, which Okhuysen and Bechky (2009, p. 474) call direct information sharing; the name Stigmergy claimed the placing that would answer the posts, which the record does not hold (serial-C5/finding-4-stigmergy-aligned.md).
refuted_by: a larger coded draw in which proposals fall below half of the bearing records of extending the work and of adding a personal piece
why: J's ruling 3 of 15 October: recut Stigmergy only if the cut joins what Grassé and Heylighen keep apart; the fleet readers at C5c-01 and the field analyst at C5c-02 coded blind, and the rule, its destinations and the three-coder combination were logged before each tally

statement: Written replies to calls to place show the same asymmetry as replies to attack calls, on few refusals, and most calls get no written reply at all. Of 80 seeded first coded replies to calls to place, 63 answer a call: 31 accept, 3 refuse, 2 are mixed and 27 take no stance. Refusals gave a reason in 3 of 3 ('I've seen too much /r/place spam today already. So...no thanks.' [polyamory/c0002]) and acceptances in 6 of 31 (one-sided Fisher p 0.014); 25 acceptances came bare ('I'll help.' [PUBATTLEGROUNDS/c0050]). In the record, 1,029 of 1,949 calls to place (0.53) and 883 of 1,565 attack calls (0.56) carry no direct reply by another member; of the direct replies written, 0.21 and 0.26 carry no coded text, and about 0.01 have a deleted author.
bound: Coded by the analyst alone under rules written before reading; first coded direct replies only, one per room. Only what was written and coded can be read: an acceptance done by placing leaves no reply, a silent refusal leaves none either, and a reply that left no coded text cannot be read for its stance. So the ratio of stances in writing is not the room's, and the refusal side rests on 3 replies.
refuted_by: a larger draw of written refusals to calls to place in which they give a reason no more often than acceptances
prompted_by: J's framing (C5c-07, C5c-11): omission against commission; what is heard less may have survived less in the record
why: problem 2 of the serial work: F-014 was counted on attack calls only, with its ratio set by its draw; this reads calls to place, and counts what of the replies survives in the coded record before the asymmetry is read

statement: In written, coded replies to attack calls, refusals mostly carry a reason and acceptances mostly come bare. Of 80 seeded reply pairs, 57 had a first part that calls for or proposes an attack. Read for stance, refusals gave a reason in 23 of 38 and acceptances in 2 of 14 (one-sided Fisher p 0.0032). Refusals were not longer (median 9.5 words against 11.5). In a refusal the reason states the room's norm or the attack's cost: 'Why? That'll just cause them to want to attack us' (uoft/c0115).
bound: Coded by the analyst alone under rules written before reading. First parts are attack calls only; calls to place were not tested. The theme a reply sits under does not track its stance, so the pairs were drawn by theme and coded by reading. Reply intervals were not read as conversation analysis's delay, since posting latency is not turn-internal delay. At C5c-11: the 38 refusals against 14 acceptances were set by the draw (up to 40 rooms per kind), not by the rooms; more than half of all calls carry no written reply, and a quarter of the written replies to attack calls carry no coded text, so the asymmetry is a fact about written, coded replies. Replies to calls to place show it too, on 3 refusals (F-023).
refuted_by: a second coder, reading the same pairs under the same rules, finding reasons about as often in acceptances as in refusals
why: stage C3b, section 4a: the distant field's prediction for the call and its answers, tested

statement: After a loss, a room that judges its hands too few either moves or gives the work up. Of the 21 rooms carrying both doubt about their hands (K02) and a move (P10), read whole, 10 voiced the judgment before the move, after a loss or erosion of the spot ('We just don't have the people.' [anarcho_capitalism/c0031], then 'Buildling ancap flag somewhere else would be a good idea' [anarcho_capitalism/c0077]); in 10 the loss itself prompted the move, and the judgment came after it or inside the move turns; 1 did not move. Of the 36 rooms that voiced such doubt and whose record says the work was lost, 10 moved, and of the 26 with no move, 11 gave the work up ('we're not doing this anymore don't do it' [raocow/c0062]), 7 voiced the doubt before any loss and 8 otherwise.
bound: Coded by the analyst alone under rules written before reading; the first three concepts of each element in each room. 10 of 20 is at the rule's line; read as a coalition's move, MiamiHurricanes makes it 9 of 20, where the rule does not decide. The judgment speaks for the room in 7 of the 10 and for one member apart in 3. work_remained is what the room's record says, not the canvas. At C5c-12 a quote was restored to the record's spelling ('Buildling'); nothing else changed.
refuted_by: a second coder, reading the same rooms under the same codes, finding the judgment before the move in fewer than a third of the rooms that moved after a loss
prompted_by: J's advice on thin evidence (C5c-07): crucial things happen rarely
why: problem 3 of the serial work (notes-C5.md, C5c-07 and C5c-08): A10 was thin on 21 rooms; every room was read whole, and the rooms that voiced doubt, lost their work and did not move were read for what they did

statement: The rooms' goals were made on the clock, mostly from a sign the room already had, proposed by one member and argued in its design rather than chosen between; a vote was rare; loss changed the goal. A member proposes the room's mark in 166 of 705 rooms (median first hour 12.7). The design is argued in 281 rooms and put to a vote in 18 (median first vote at hour 42.4; 7 of 18 before hour 24). The goal is inherited in 152 rooms: the homeland's flag 96, national emblems 39, the room's mark found already placed 43, a sign others began adopted 6. It is contested in 152, mostly over whether the canvas belongs in the host sub at all (arguing the canvas's worth 76, objecting to the canvas flood 72). It is changed in 190: relocating 116, upkeep chosen over expansion 43, fewer pieces 29, quitting 20, weighing fight against move 17. The structure places the making of the goal in Collective representation (T4-006) and the model in the room settling its mark (P02) and the starter (R01), outside the four problems, which take the goal as given. The goal is a picture, so one artifact can state it and divide it (A11, theorised); at room level an argued design goes with shared coordinates only slightly more often (94 of 281 rooms, against 113 of the other 424; not held to size).
bound: The four modes are the analyst's placement of third-order themes by their names; the theme a record sits under does not track its stance, so the counts are of rooms whose coded talk sits under a theme, not of rooms read for how they chose. The modes overlap (a room can inherit a flag and argue its design). Counts are not held to size. A goal set in a chat or before the canvas is invisible here, and the claim that goals were rarely chosen between rivals is an absence claim, marked weak.
refuted_by: a read of the rooms' first proposals showing that most goals were chosen against a rival proposal, or set by a body outside the room
why: stage C3c, section 5, part 5: whether each room inherited, negotiated, contested or changed its goal, the question C3a left open from Felin and Zenger Re-examined at D3a-01 (rule 14): against move 172, which split the joining clause from R01 and left it to P15, A02 and A01. F-017 counts members proposing the room's mark (166 rooms) and places the making of the goal in T4-006, P02 and R01; R01 still names the member who proposes, so no count, placement or bound changes. Unchanged.

statement: Keepers repair a change the room has planned or agreed (P02) away as damage until they learn of it. P05, frozen at D3c, names one route to that knowledge, the telling, and holds that the change is lost or given up where the telling does not reach the keepers. The re-check of all 705 rooms shows two more routes by which the change outlasts the missing telling: in six rooms the keepers read the change from its shape and stop repairing it ('once it reached a critical mass and people saw what it was they just naturally began protecting it instead of destroying it' [halo/c0402]), and in three informed members hold it against keepers who do not know.
bound: The told route, P05's frozen clause, holds where the keepers can learn of a planned change only by being told and no informed member holds it. It does not hold in nine rooms whose re-check correction the ledger accepts. In completeanarchy, polska, satania, halo, bangtan and thesilphroad the keepers read the change from its shape before anyone tells them; this is a cluster branch, 'the shape read', warranted at D3b by two pairs meeting at one node (polska and satania at T4-006, halo and bangtan at T4-019), and carried to D4 and D5, where branches are built and judged. In armok, maryland and oneshot informed members hold the change against keepers who do not know; these are paired corrections at three nodes, below the trigger, named here as a second limit. P05's four cause rooms (OnePiece, leagueoflegends, monsterhunter, portugal) carry no correction of the clause. 25 absent lines in 25 rooms leave the clause untested. The element's words are unchanged in the frozen model (QD3-011, option b); the revision drafted at D3b is held for D4.
refuted_by: a room whose keepers knew of a planned change, by being told or by reading its shape, and kept repairing it away as damage
a room where the change could not be read from its shape, no one told the keepers and no informed member held it, and the change still stood
why: the scope decision for P05's added clause under QD3-011 (J, 23 October, 10:36 Berlin: option b; freeze 46384686, hold the move): a claim corrected locally cannot remain universal globally without a scope decision (rule 12); no finding touched P05, so the bounded claim is a new finding (rule 14)

statement: P05 holds that a change the room has planned or agreed is repaired away as damage until its keepers are told of it. The clause presumes that the keepers would accept the change once told. In 31 of the 59 rooms of branch F07 a re-check line says that informed members rejected the change, so that repair enforced a competing design and telling did not settle it; in 20 of them the line names no evidence limit. In r/AyyMD a member was told the poll result ('there was a poll , the logo stays GREEN' [AyyMD/c0109]) and another answered 'And those people are wrong' [AyyMD/c0137]. In r/katawashoujo the original builders, told of a purple background, kept black [katawashoujo/c0037], and the proposer yielded [katawashoujo/c0042].
bound: The telling clause holds where the keepers would accept the planned change once they know of it. It does not explain repair where informed members reject the change: there the repair is a contest over the design, which telling does not end. In 36 of F07's 59 rooms, 11 of them among the 31, a re-check line says the record does not show the agreed change, the untold keepers, the failed telling or the loss, so the clause is untested there. F-024's two routes (the change read from its shape, informed members holding it) are not touched. The element's words are unchanged in the frozen model; this is a finding, not an amendment, and D6 may act on it.
why: Rule 14: a claim a branch bounds is a findings line (stage D5, section 5). The bound rests on the members' re-check lines and on their words through cite.py, not on the cut of the branch.
refuted_by: a room whose informed members rejected a planned change and then stopped repairing it once told, without a change of design or a decision

statement: P05 holds that a change the room has planned or agreed is repaired away as damage until its keepers are told of it, and that it is lost or given up where the telling does not reach them. At a border the planned change belongs to an agreement between two rooms. In branch F26 (23 rooms, cut on a restrict line on P05 at the theme of settling borders with neighbours), members' cited words show both halves of the clause. Told keepers stopped: 'I'll stop. :)' [placetardis/c0022]; 'Me and my throwaways will stop resisting now.' [placeportalpattern/c0054]; 'Okay, we are going to stop fiddling with your flag and you continue. Thanks for filling us in.' [NewMexico/c0057]; also r/python [python/c0098] and r/metroid [metroid/c0126]. Where the telling did not reach, the change was fought or lost: 'We tried to make Crash work, too many randoms weren't clued in sadly.' [NewMexico/c0062]; 'some of ours haven't gotten the memo' [stevenuniverse/c0308]. And members who knew the terms refused them. In 10 of the 23 rooms a re-check line says so; in r/buffalobills the member who had stated the compromise [buffalobills/c0046] later wrote 'DOWN WITH THE BORDER' [buffalobills/c0048], and in r/stevenuniverse, after a neighbour reported a move agreed by the room's diplomats [stevenuniverse/c0409], a member answered 'I don't give a fuck about peace' [stevenuniverse/c0410].
bound: F-025's limit holds at the border: the telling clause settles a planned change only where those told accept it. At the border the clause needs two more things. The news must cross from where the agreement was made, often a chat, to the placers of both rooms ('Problem is how many Norwegians don't know about Discord plans or peace accords I'm afraid.' [stevenuniverse/c0362]). And members of either room can know the terms and refuse them, so a repair or a crossing of the line may be an untold keeper's or an informed refusal, and the two look the same on the canvas. In 17 of F26's 23 rooms the re-check line says the record does not show the clause's parts, while the cited words show the first half in at least five rooms and the second in two; the lines understate what the members' words show. F-024's two routes and F-025 are not touched. The element's words are unchanged in the frozen model; this is a finding, not an amendment, and D6 may act on it.
why: Rule 14: a claim a branch bounds is a findings line (stage D5, section 5). The bound rests on the members' re-check lines and on their words through cite.py, not on the cut of the branch.
refuted_by: a room whose informed members refused an agreed border and then stopped undoing it once told again, without a change of the terms or a decision of the room
an agreed border change that held although the placers of the room it changed are shown not to have been told

statement: P05 holds that repair restores the form the keepers know, so that a change the room has planned or agreed is repaired away as damage until its keepers are told of it, and is lost or given up where the telling does not reach them. In branch F27 (27 rooms, cut on a restrict line on P05 at the theme of repair work), the re-check lines say that interference is shown and that its cause and the loss are not. Members' cited words show the cause: in at least eight rooms they say keepers took a change for damage or had not been told ('I fell into that trap myself and actively worked against fixing the jaw all the while believing I was doing the right thing.' [OnePiece/c0232]; 'A lot of it was anti-griefers who thought the hole was caused by griefing.' [cowchop/c0073]; 'I'm in voice chat right now and was thinking that the blue was vandalism.' [wholesomememes/c0161]; also r/armok [armok/c0054], r/frc [frc/c0084], r/sixers [sixers/c0107], r/empiredidnothingwrong [empiredidnothingwrong/c0128] and r/parahumans [parahumans/c0157]). In six rooms the change undone was one member's correction toward the room's own design, not a change the room had planned ('It's meant to touch the period, people.' [metalcore/c0126]; also r/OnePiece, r/hawks, r/hellointernet, r/empiredidnothingwrong and r/toolband). In four rooms scripts kept the old form until their operators changed them ('it was the script sorry' [hellointernet/c0129]; also r/armok, r/greece and r/turkey). Where a cited passage gives the end of a change repaired in error, the change was made late (r/OnePiece's jaw), kept to the close ('(With the holes, too!)' bound: In keeping, the clause's first part holds more widely than its words. Repair restores the form the keepers last saw, so a member's correction toward the room's own design is repaired away as damage, as a planned change is; this is P05's own sentence 'Repair restores the form the keepers know' at work, and it does not need a change the room planned or agreed. Telling reaches a script only through its operator. The clause's second part, the loss of a change for want of telling, is not shown in F27's cited passages: the ends shown are delay, survival to the close, and abandonment by informed choice. 'Not shown' is not 'absent': the claim is about these 27 rooms' cited passages, and the re-check lines in 12 of them say the loss is not shown. F-024, F-025 and F-026 are not touched. The element's words are unchanged in the frozen model; this is a finding, not an amendment, and D6 may act on it.
why: Rule 14: a claim a branch bounds is a findings line (stage D5, section 5). The bound rests on the members' re-check lines and on their words through cite.py, not on the cut of the branch.
